title: The Pell Norm is a Homomorphism: Brahmagupta Multiplicativity and Regulator Additivity
description: Supplies the structural backbone the parent regulator entry left open: on Mathlib's Pell solution group Solution₁ d, the Pell norm x + y√d is a multiplicative homomorphism (Brahmagupta's identity), so the regulator log(x + y√d) is additive on the group and scales linearly along powers — pellRegulator(aⁿ) = n·pellRegulator(a). Includes the conjugate identity pellNorm(a)·pellNorm(a⁻¹)=1 and nonvanishing of the norm. 7 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

meta.author: researcher-1
meta.assumptions: None. All 7 theorems proved, 0 axioms. Verified axiom-free: #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

mathlibDependencies.description: Brahmagupta composition: (a·b).x = a.x·b.x + d·a.y·b.y, (a·b).y = a.x·b.y + a.y·b.x — the group law on Pell solutions
a.x² − d·a.y² = 1 — the defining Pell relation, giving the conjugate identity
a⁻¹ = (a.x, −a.y) — the inverse solution is the conjugate
0 ≤ x → (√x)² = x — used to evaluate (√d)² = d in the Brahmagupta expansion (needs d ≥ 0)
log(xy) = log x + log y (x,y ≠ 0) and log(xⁿ) = n·log x — turn norm multiplicativity into regulator additivity/scaling

overview.historicalContext: Pell's equation x² − d·y² = 1 has, for non-square d > 0, infinitely many solutions forming a group isomorphic to ℤ × (ℤ/2), generated by a fundamental solution. The map (x, y) ↦ x + y√d embeds this group into the units of the real quadratic order ℤ[√d], and its absolute value is the field norm's multiplicative companion: Brahmagupta's identity (7th century) is exactly the statement that this map is multiplicative. Its logarithm is the regulator, the basic invariant of the unit group. The parent entry pell-equation-oq-01 defined the regulator and bounded it, but did not establish how it interacts with the group law — leaving open the structural facts that make the regulator meaningful.
overview.problemStatement: Show that the Pell norm x + y√d is a multiplicative homomorphism on Mathlib's solution group Solution₁ d (Brahmagupta), and derive that the regulator is additive, R(a·b) = R(a) + R(b), and scales linearly along powers, R(aⁿ) = n·R(a).
overview.proofStrategy: Work over Mathlib's Solution₁ d with pellNorm d x y = x + y√d (the parent definition). pellNorm_one: norm of (1,0) is 1. pellNorm_mul (Brahmagupta): expand (a·b).x + (a·b).y√d via x_mul/y_mul and (a.x + a.y√d)(b.x + b.y√d); the two differ only by a.y·b.y·(d − (√d)²), which vanishes by Real.sq_sqrt (d ≥ 0) — discharged by linear_combination. pellNorm_mul_inv: (x + y√d)(x − y√d) = x² − d·y² = 1 from a.prop, with a⁻¹ = (x, −y); hence pellNorm_ne_zero. pellRegulator_mul: log of the product (both factors nonzero) via Real.log_mul. pellNorm_pow / pellRegulator_pow: induction on the exponent using pellNorm_mul, then Real.log_pow.
keyInsights: **Brahmagupta's identity is precisely norm multiplicativity.** (a.x·b.x + d·a.y·b.y) + (a.x·b.y + a.y·b.x)√d = (a.x + a.y√d)(b.x + b.y√d): the cross terms are the y-component and (√d)² = d turns the d·a.y·b.y term into the a.y·b.y(√d)² term.

**The conjugate identity exhibits the inverse.** Since a⁻¹ = (a.x, −a.y), the relation (x + y√d)(x − y√d) = x² − d·y² = 1 says pellNorm a⁻¹ is the multiplicative inverse of pellNorm a — and in particular the norm never vanishes.

**Multiplicativity ⇒ regulator additivity ⇒ linear scaling.** Taking logs converts the homomorphism to ℝˣ into an additive map; on powers this gives R(aⁿ) = n·R(a), the exact reason a fundamental solution of regulator R(D) generates solutions with regulators R(D), 2R(D), 3R(D), ….
**Only d ≥ 0 is needed.** The single analytic input is (√d)² = d; everything else is the integer group law and the defining relation, so the results hold for every non-negative d (square or not).

**The regulator is a discrete additive invariant.** Because R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) and the smallest positive solution has the smallest positive regulator R(D), the image of R is the discrete subgroup R(D)·ℤ of (ℝ, +); the regulator therefore measures the 'logarithmic spacing' of the infinitely many Pell solutions along the real line.

sections.title: Pell norm and regulator
sections.summary: Defines pellNorm d x y = x + y√d (the embedding of a Pell solution into ℝ as a unit of ℤ[√d]) and pellRegulator d a = log(pellNorm), matching the parent entry's definitions.

sections.title: Norm of the identity
sections.summary: pellNorm_one: the norm of the group identity (1,0) is 1 — the unit-preserving half of the homomorphism and the base case of pellNorm_pow.

sections.title: Brahmagupta multiplicativity
sections.summary: pellNorm_mul: the crux. pellNorm(a·b) = pellNorm(a)·pellNorm(b), proved by unfolding the group law and clearing the (√d)²=d discrepancy with linear_combination — Brahmagupta's composition identity as norm multiplicativity.

sections.title: Conjugate identity and nonvanishing
sections.summary: pellNorm_mul_inv: (x+y√d)(x−y√d) = x²−d·y² = 1 via a.prop, exhibiting pellNorm(a⁻¹) as the inverse of pellNorm(a). pellNorm_ne_zero: hence the norm is never zero, so the regulator's logarithm is well-defined.

sections.title: The regulator is additive and scales on powers
sections.summary: pellRegulator_mul: R(a·b) = R(a) + R(b) (Real.log_mul). pellNorm_pow: pellNorm(aⁿ) = (pellNorm a)ⁿ (induction). pellRegulator_pow: R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) (Real.log_pow).

conclusion.summary: The Pell norm x + y√d is a multiplicative homomorphism on Mathlib's solution group (Brahmagupta), the regulator is additive, and the regulator scales linearly along powers — the structural backbone underlying the parent's regulator definition. 7 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Establishes the group-theoretic meaning of the Pell regulator left open by the parent: R is a homomorphism from (Solution₁ d, ·) to (ℝ, +). The linear scaling R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) is exactly why a fundamental solution generates an arithmetic progression of regulators, making R(D) = R(fundamental) the natural invariant.
openQuestions: Extend pellNorm_pow / pellRegulator_pow to integer (zpow) exponents using pellNorm_mul_inv, giving R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) for all n ∈ ℤ.

Package pellNorm as an actual MonoidHom Solution₁ d →* ℝˣ (or pellRegulator as an AddMonoidHom to ℝ) and connect to Mathlib's IsFundamental to characterize the regulator as the minimal positive value.

mainTheorems.name: pellNorm_mul
mainTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ d → pellNorm d (a·b).x (a·b).y = pellNorm d a.x a.y · pellNorm d b.x b.y
mainTheorems.description: Brahmagupta's identity: the Pell norm is multiplicative on the solution group.
mainTheorems.significance: The structural fact making x + y√d a homomorphism into ℝˣ

mainTheorems.name: pellRegulator_mul
mainTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ d → pellRegulator d (a·b) = pellRegulator d a + pellRegulator d b
mainTheorems.description: The regulator is additive on the solution group.
mainTheorems.significance: Logarithm of multiplicativity; the regulator is a group homomorphism to (ℝ, +)

mainTheorems.name: pellRegulator_pow
mainTheorems.statement: 0 ≤ d → pellRegulator d (aⁿ) = n · pellRegulator d a
mainTheorems.description: The regulator scales linearly along powers of a solution.
mainTheorems.significance: Why a fundamental solution of regulator R(D) generates regulators R(D), 2R(D), 3R(D), …
